comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support pubget's functionality and implementation (C10-C11, C42, C52-C69, C94). OpenEval emphasizes technical details and successful integration, while peer reviewers highlight the tool's value for large-scale analyses and public accessibility. Strong agreement on tool capabilities.

Both evaluations support labelbuddy's design and functionality (C70-C78). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of features like SQLite storage and cross-platform binaries, while peer reviewers praise it as a 'charm' for text annotation and confirm public accessibility. Strong agreement on tool quality.

Significant disagreement on brain map comparison claims (C18-C20, C97-C100). OpenEval finds these supported by Figure 3 visual evidence, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically noting 'the results from the litmining ecosystem were not validated' and requesting comparison with recognized ground truth.

Disagreement on validation methodology (C25-C33, C82-C88). OpenEval considers the train/validation split and reported metrics as appropriate support, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating results 'were not validated' against recognized ground truth despite internal validation efforts.

Both support the demographic findings (C34-C38, C112). OpenEval notes some interpretations are speculative but overall supported by Figure 4B-C. Peer reviewers affirm the findings without challenge, noting 'solid and validated methodology' for data collection. Agreement on descriptive findings.

Both support the dFC analysis findings (C40-C41, C113-C120). OpenEval finds conclusions follow directly from Figure 6 data. Peer reviewers do not challenge findings and note the examples help readers understand tool applications. Strong agreement on this use case demonstration.

Both support the annotation repository statistics (C101-C109). OpenEval notes these are straightforward data summaries with internally consistent numbers. Peer reviewers confirm repository accessibility and do not challenge the reported statistics from Table 1.

Disagreement on comparative evaluation claims (C89-C93). OpenEval finds the design goals and Figure 1 comparisons reasonable and justified. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting quantitative indices to prove efficiency rather than accepting qualitative assessments.

Both support the Open Access limitation acknowledgment (C43-C46). OpenEval finds the justification sound with optimistic outlook supported by policy citations. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this limitation, with one stating outcomes are 'constrained by inherent limitations.' Agreement on limitation and rationale.

Both support real-world adoption claims (C50-C51, C110-C111). OpenEval notes concrete use cases demonstrate utility beyond illustrative examples. Peer reviewers do not challenge the claims and note the ecosystem is 'relatively mature,' consistent with broader adoption. Agreement on demonstrated impact.

Both support background/context claims (C64-C65 overlap). OpenEval finds these standard background claims accurately represent prior work. Peer reviewers do not challenge the NiMARE characterization. Agreement on contextual claims, though OpenEval R11 covers broader background (C1-C16) not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R11 covers extensive background claims (C1-C9, C12-C16) establishing context through literature citations that have no corresponding separate peer review evaluation. These foundational claims about literature mining challenges and prior work are implicitly accepted but not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on labelbuddy repository structure (C79-C81, C96). OpenEval evaluates these as part of labelbuddy's overall design assessment. Peer reviewers address repository accessibility in context of annotation statistics. Both support these claims but group them differently.

Partial overlap on Open Access justification (C47-C49). OpenEval R9 evaluates these as part of limitation discussion, finding the trade-off justified. Peer R8 addresses these in context of comparative evaluation, rating UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantitative validation. Different framing of related claims.
